annotations.text:
A — ANALOG TICKET

Cream stock, ink-stamped rating, condensed grotesque with mono metadata. Treats a Kreami as a stub you kept: a physical verdict with a date on it.

Why it might win: most distinctive of the three, and it screenshots like an object rather than a UI. The mono numerals give the score real authority.

Tradeoff: the retro-analog register is a strong flavor to commit to. It can read as effortful, and condensed type is the least forgiving of long topic titles at small sizes.

B — EDITORIAL

Hairline rules instead of cards, serif display for titles and numerals, one burgundy accent, a lot of air. Entries sit on the page like a review column.

Why it might win: the deadpan works best here. 'Jury duty, 0/5' is funnier set seriously than set playfully, and the restraint ages well.

Tradeoff: the quietest of the three. Less thumb-stopping in a feed, and the generous whitespace means fewer Kreamis per screen — which matters when density is what makes the feed feel alive.

C — CANDY POP

Chunky black outlines, hard offset shadows, rounded geometric type, three same-chroma accents. Every card is an object you want to poke.

Why it might win: most obviously fun, highest contrast in a feed, and the easiest to build a recognizable brand from. Reads instantly as 'not a serious review site.'

Tradeoff: the loudest and the fastest to date — this style is everywhere right now. Risks reading as a kids' app, and the heavy chrome competes with the rating for attention.
